newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up 8.65 pct on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up 8.65 pct on foreign buying.

text.p: Thai stocks closed sharply higher for the second day in a row on Thursday, jumping 8.65 percent as foreigners bought cheap blue-chip stocks after the government changed the baht to a managed float system, brokers said.
"Foreigners rushed to buy stocks, including small issues, across the board today. It's very strange," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
The composite SET index rose 49.19 points to 617.98 on 8.7 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index advanced 3.99 points to 45.73.

The flotation, which was announced on Wednesday, effectively devalued the baht by between 15-20 percent as the central bank dropped its pegged rate system against a basket of currencies and allowed market forces to determine the rate.
"Foreigners seemed to buy every stock today as they thought Thai stocks were cheap now. I think the buying was also probably aimed at short-term speculation," said Bunsom.
Brokers said Wednesday's announcement also erased previous uncertainty and concerns by foreigners caused by persistent market rumours of a baht devaluation.
